correctness.rationale: Von Neumann trace alignment shows that for a fixed admissible pentagon M=sum Pj the state expectation max equals a m1+b m2. The known complete pentagram characteristic polynomial parametrizes all spectra by z=m1 in [2,sqrt5]. Solving for r and the remaining eigenvalue discriminant gives D(z)=(z-1)(5-z²)/(3-z) and m2=(5-z+sqrt(D))/2. D>0 on (2,sqrt5), D''(z)=2(z-1)(z²-8z+19)/(z-3)^3<0, so for b>0 the objective f(z)=az+(b/2)(5-z+sqrt D) is strictly concave. At z=2 f'=a-b and as z approaches sqrt5 f'→-infinity. Interior 0<b<a therefore has exactly one global maximizer, and N(z)<0 removes extraneous roots upon squaring stationarity to the sextic equation q²N²=(z-1)(5-z²)(3-z)³. Endpoints b=0 yield sqrt5, a=b=1/2 yield 2. Five explicit normalized real rays satisfy cyclic orthogonality and realize every spectral parameter, hence the upper bound is attained even allowing complex projectors. An independent exact symbolic projector characteristic polynomial and derivative check corroborated the analytic proof.
